General Awards Passed By The Third Respondent Bearing
No.Kiadb/Laq/1385/2022-23, Dated 12/01/2023 And Another
General Ward Bearing No.Kiadb/Laq/1396/2022-23 Dated
12/01/2023 Instead Of Passing A Consent Award, Which Are
Produced Herewith For The Kind Perusal Of This Honble
Court And Marked As Annexure - M And N As Illegal,
Arbitrary, Capricious, Discriminatory And The Same Is
Passed Without Application Of Mind. 2.

Directing The R2
And R3 To Pass The Consent Award In Place Of Or Instead
Of General Award Dated 12/01/2023 As Done In Several
Other Similar Cases And Etc.,
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
1. To issue a writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ, Order or Direction,
quashing an impugned General Awards passed by the third respondent bearing NO.
KIADB.LAQ/1385/2022-23 dated 12.01.2023 and another General Award bearing No.KIADB.LA/1396/2022-23 dt.12.01.2023 instead of passing a Consent award which are produced herewith for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court and marked as Annexures - M & N as illegal,
arbitrary, capricious, discriminatory and same is passed without application of mind;
2. To issue a Writ of mandamus in the nature of order/direction, directing the respondents no.2 and 3 to pass the consent award in place of or instead of General Award dated 12.01.2023 as done in several other similar cases in the interest of justice and equity etc.

Sri Fayaz Sab B.G., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner's father-in-law one Sri Veerabhadraiah @ Muddappa was propositus of Hindu undivided Joint family, died in year 1980 leaving behind his five sons.

After his death properties were partitioned among brothers under Smt. Rudramma K vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184215758/
2 registered partition deed dated 22.09.2008 and schedule 'A' property bearing Sy.no.37/4 measuring 0.05 guntas, situated at Obalapura village (Hadihosahalli village) Thyamagondlu Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, fell to share of husband of petitioner.

entities.text: Smt. Rudramma K vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After his death on 11.06.2019, petitioner became absolute owner of schedule 'A' property and her name was entered in revenue records.

3. It was further submitted that 'schedule B' property measuring 15 guntas in Sy.no.32/1 of same village was purchased by petitioner under registered sale deed dated 22.01.1991 and she became owner of said property.

In meanwhile, respondent authority acquired same for purpose of Multi Modal Logistics Park and passed General award on 12.01.2023.
4.

It was submitted that though petitioner was entitled to higher compensation under consent award, without offering NC: 2023:KHC:44386 opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO).

It was contended that under consent award,
compensation was considerably higher than under General Award and failure to offer same to petitioner was illegal.
Therefore, General award was under challenge.
It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court allowed several writ petitions, including W.P.no.24733/2023.

disposed of on 09.11.2023,
quashed General Award and directed consideration for passing consent award
Relying upon same, learned counsel for petitioner sought for granting similar relief.

5. On other hand, Sri Manjunath V Rayappa, learned AGA , for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V.
Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that general award was passed as petitioner had failed to file application for consent award.
In view of earlier decisions, if petitioner submits representation, respondent no.3 would consider same, in accordance with law within reasonable time.

6. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
NC: 2023:KHC:44386 7.

From above, it is seen that failure to pass consent award is due to non-filing of application by petitioner and in W.P.No.24733/2023, this Court under similar circumstances had quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply to this case also.

8. Accordingly, Writ petition is disposed of, impugned General Awards bearing no.KIADB.LAQ/1385/2022-23 dated 12.01.2023 and no.KIADB.LA/1396/2022-23 dated 12.01.2023 at Annexures- M and N passed by respondent no.3 in respect of petitioner's land
, are quashed.

9. Respondent no.3 is directed to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act within a period of three months from date of receipt of certified copy of this Smt. Rudramma K vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184215758/
3 order.
Needless to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as a positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.
